title: Retelling the trip to New Orleans before Kid Ross
summary: Asked about Kid Ross, Williams starts over the freight-train journey until Gerdy reminds him he already told it.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Kid Ross was a piano player that, uh, well let me tell you how I come in town.

I left home and went to Philadelphia, bought a streetcar, went to Baltimore for two cents a mile on the Baltimore, Ohio. The fella gave me a job, and I got a buck that night, and I, uh, decided to take his streetcar, and the freight train is blocking us. He's just dragging. Now, what the hell made me in the mind to get out? And I got out and grabbed that train. And I went to, uh, uh, what do they call it, Maryland. And I took an elder named that had a branch on it into Louisville. Well, I'm born in Louisville. Uncle Sis and Aunt this.
Wait a minute. You done told that once before you're coming back.
Oh, wait a minute. I don't hear it. What do you say?
You told that once before you're coming back for the same thing you want to know about Kid Ross.
I'm going to tell him how I got to New Orleans.
You told him that before, didn't he?
Did I tell you about going to Jackson, Tennessee?
But you were going to tell us about Kid Ross.
